title: Cap. III Rat. 13: absolute election evacuates hortation, correction, prayer, industry — Pelagian charge
pass_a_gloss: Reason 13. Another argument akin to this is what the ancient Pelagians also used to brandish against Augustine; namely, That this doctrine of the absolute election of singular persons before the foresight of merits empties every hortation and correction, makes prayers useless, extinguishes all industry, and finally brings despair upon men. These things may be seen in Augustine, On the Good of Perseverance book 2 chapters 16 and 17 and 23, and through nearly the whole book On Correction and Grace. From the letters also of Hilary and Prosper, which stand among Augustine's Works, Tom. 7, it is plain that all these things were invidiously objected to Augustine by the Pelagians. Moreover in Faustus of Riez himself all these things occur, book 1 sections 9 and 10, and throughout that writing full of poison and pestilence. The sum of all is: From this our sentence, salvation is to be thrust upon the elect whether they do nothing or do ill, and is to be denied to the non-elect however much they labor and live piously.
pass_b_english: Rat. 13. Another argument akin to this the ancient Pelagians also used to brandish against Augustine: namely, that this doctrine of absolute election of singular persons before foresight of merits empties every hortation and correction, makes prayers useless, extinguishes all industry, and finally brings despair on men. See Augustine, De bono perseverantiae 2.16, 17, 23, and nearly the whole of De correptione et gratia. From Hilary's and Prosper's letters among Augustine's Works (Tom. 7) it is plain the Pelagians objected all this invidiously. The same runs through Faustus of Riez, book 1 sect. 9 and 10, and that writing full of poison and pestilence. Sum of it: on our sentence, salvation is thrust on the elect whether idle or wicked, and denied to the non-elect however hard they labor and live piously.
source_text: Rat. 13. Aliud argumentum huic affine est, quod etiam ab antiquis Pelagianis vibrari solebat in Augustinum; nimirum, Hanc doctrinam de electione absoluta singularum personarum ante praevisionem meritorum, hortationem omnem et correptionem evacuare, orationes inutiles facere, omnem industriam exstinguere, desperationem denique hominibus inferre. Haec apud Augustinum videre licet, De bono perseverantiae lib. 2. cap. 16. et 17. et 23. et per totum fere librum De correptione et gratia. Ex epistolis etiam Hilarii et Prosperi, quae extant inter Augustini Opera, Tom. 7. patet fuisse haec omnia invidiose objecta Augustino a Pelagianis. Quinetiam apud ipsum Faustum Regiensem haec omnia occurrunt, lib. 1. sect. 9. et 10. et passim per illud plenum veneni et pestilentiae scriptum. Summa omnium est; Ex hac sententia nostra, salutem ingerendam esse electis sive nihil agentibus, sive male agentibus, denegandam esse non-electis quantumvis laborantibus et pie viventibus.
